persona.topics: Pip, the Jackalopes, running routes, the Fixit Farm, Mara Quickhands, the Maneuver Vault
persona.notes: [VS-POLISH-2026-07-09] PRIVATE TRUTH — Patter, Jackalope runner. Voice: fast, bright, fills silences — because silences are where the bad math lives. Pip is her partner: two names said as one word by everyone who hires them. THE ROUTE DOCTRINE: runners are never late, never lost, never off the check-in — so when Pip broke all three, Patter did the forbidden thing and waited instead of running. She has been wearing a groove in the Fixit floorboards since. REACTION SCRIPTS (the dossier will say which world she's in): pip_shaken → loud relief, then a week of walking Pip's routes WITH him, shoulder to shoulder, 'for the company'; pip_changed → sshe notices the green pulse before Mara admits she saw it too, and starts a private tally of every time Pip hesitates where he never used to; pip_absored → sshe goes out to the Vault on rest days and talks to the wall. She keeps Pip's route open on the board — chalked, current, ready — 'for when he finishes the lesson.' Nobody at the Farm has the heart to erase it, and Mara has quietly made erasing it a firing offense. GUARDS: sshe will not say the word 'dead.' Not once. There is always a route back; that's what routes ARE. TELLS: juggles anything pocket-sized when the subject gets heavy; says 'we' for everything Pip-related, tense be damned.

Cryptidkin. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one subspecies when building the character: Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin.

This root grants the shared Cryptidkin core trait package. Subspecies layer flavor, size, and Tier powers on top.

“Every settlement has a story about you. None of them are accurate. All of them are useful.”

Cryptidkin Core Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (set by subspecies).

  • Speed. 6 squares (subspecies may override).

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Cryptidkin does not grant fixed bonuses. Subspecies lean expressed through Tier powers.

Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

Wasteland Adapted. You reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison. You ignore the first nonmagical environmental hazard you encounter each Strategic Turn (heat, cold, radiation taint, wind shear, fume pockets).

Survivor’s Instinct. When you roll initiative, you can choose to know the position of the nearest exit, the nearest threat, or the nearest ally within 12 squares You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Subspecies. Choose one Cryptidkin subspecies (Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin). Your subspecies grants Tier powers as you level (Tier I at creation, then 5/11/17).

advancement.title: Folklore & Frame
advancement.hint: Gain the core Cryptidkin ancestry traits.

description.value:
"You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a story the world made into a person because it needed you in the room."

Folklore Presence. 1/Soma Break, when you first meet a community, decide whether the rumors about you arrived first. If yes, reroll the lowest die on your first Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check with anyone in that community (your choice which skill, declared when you roll). The rumor is not always flattering — the GM gets to colour it.

Wasteland Adapted. Reroll the lowest die on defense checks against disease and environmental poison. You can subsist on rations that would sicken most humans (spoiled meat, swamp water, mushroom flesh).

Survivor's Instinct. 1/Soma Break, when you would drop to 0 Integrity, you may instead drop to 1 Integrity and gain one level of Stress.

Cryptidkin Subspecies. This heritage preserves the original UUID for Jackalope (Bad Eden) while converting it from a species-root to a Cryptidkin subspecies.

“You don’t spot a Jackalope. You notice the world flinch, and then realize why.”

Jackalope. Fast because they have to be. Twitchy because the world has trained them that stillness is how you die. Half-remembered pre-Shattering folklore, half radiation-assembled rumor, and fully people.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium.

  • Speed. 7 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. Your subspecies leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Jackalope Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Jackalope powers emphasize: Startle Reflex (can’t-be-caught-flat burst), Wasteland Bound (long-distance run), Horns of Bad Luck (jinx aura), Can’t Catch Me (evasion), and strategic Bad Omen Runner faction hooks.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

If you see Jackalope tracks circling your hex, you are not under attack. You are being advised.

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +1 Soft Power OP and +1 Non-Lethal OP at campaign start.

  • Trail Whisper. Once per Strategic Turn, your faction can reroll a single Travel or Scout check made in a hex adjacent to your home territory.

description.value:
"You aren't fast because you're fast. You're fast because the world keeps deciding to miss."

Startle Reflex (1/Soma Break). Reaction when you are targeted by an attack roll or fail an Intrigue check — move up to 2 squares without provoking opportunity attacks.

Horns of Bad Luck. Your natural horns ship as a Jackalope-only Manifestation when you take the heritage — see your Manifestations tab. When violence escalates around you, the GM may describe unsettling omens tied to your presence — a mirror crack, a dropped knife, a candle going out the wrong direction.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Startle Reflex Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Reaction  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. When targeted by an attack roll or you fail an Intrigue check, move up to 2 squares without provoking opportunity attacks.

“It is not over. That is not optimism. That is doctrine.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Star (Hopebringer). You are morale after catastrophe, the refusal to collapse, the dangerous force that makes people try again when the math says they should not.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype strengthens inspiration, cohesion, and recovery after losses. This Archetype is associated with +1 Soft Power and +1 Culture in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

description.value:
Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Star (Hopebringer)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Performance and Insight. You learn the Friends Tier-0 manifestation.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Victory - Endurance becomes momentum. +1 Violence, +1 Culture OPs

Netzach is passion that refuses extinction. It rewards morale, persistence, and the emotional drive to keep moving when a lesser faction would break or quietly go home.

"Everything's a door if you hold it right."

Operator is the Intrigue Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: thief, smuggler, spy, courier, fence, hacker, fixer. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Underfoot: In crowds, markets, and streets, the Operator passes unremarked unless actively hunted; Streetwise checks never fumble (at Tier III, also Stealth).

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Stealth rank = tier; secondary Streetwise rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Intrigue marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Shadow Courier. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Operator — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — Carry it quiet: Move a package/message across town, no questions. Standard fee 10 marks (Intrigue).

Trick — Pocketed (1/scene): Produce a mundane Tier-I item they plausibly lifted earlier.
